dossier.deep_context:
# 2018-254 — The Cheesy Poofs: LOCKDOWN

A compact six-wheel drivebase carries a pass-through, continuously rigged elevator and wristed compliant-wheel cube intake. The elevator changes gearing between rapid scoring travel and lifting two robots. A spring-deployed hook and partner forklift create a shared endgame load path. Motion planning coordinates intake, wrist and elevator; a driver-station camera estimates scale attitude.

## Strategic interpretation

The team explicitly connects world-championship ambition to first seed, low partner dependence, all-target scoring, a multi-cube scale auto and a partner lift. The historical robot shows that broad primary capability can coexist with a matchup-specific switch assignment. For 1833, extract passive/compliant geometry and electric motion architecture; the original pneumatic shifting, hook retention and fork deployment require redesign, and historical sub-second claims are not current acceptance evidence.

## Low-profile sprint chassis and gearbox

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [10, 11].

### Published construction or code

The binder specifies a six-wheel West Coast layout with center drop, two nitrile traction wheels and four omnis. A flat three-MiniCIM gearbox arrangement lowers the package beneath the intake. The middle pinion receives an additional bearing plate rather than remaining unsupported against the other motors. Two drive ratios are published, along with wheel sizes and nominal speeds.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

The team lists short-sprint acceleration, maneuverability, platform clearance and resisting defense as design goals, while a wide wheelbase accommodates a raised load and a partner.

### Engineering interpretation

The valuable feature is integration: lowering the gearbox also lowers the intake rest position, which changes acquisition geometry. Moving the pickup upward to clear motors would impose a new lifting/rolling transition on every cube. Omnis can reduce scrub while traction placement still matters for pushing and ramp contact. A new chassis must evaluate the actual support polygon and loaded CG, not copy the wheel count as a performance recipe. Reported high-gear free speed does not establish defended acceleration or stopping distance.

### Proposed validation — not performed

First check intake rest height and field-obstacle breakover in a section view. Then calculate traction/current-limited acceleration and the raised-load tipping boundary; test only the uncertain transition if it can change the layout.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Sprint chassis](../../images/history_2018-254_p10.jpg)

![Flat drive gearbox](../../images/history_2018-254_p11.jpg)

## Compliant jaws and reversible wrist scoring

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [14].

### Published construction or code

Opposed wheel groups sit on polycarbonate jaw plates. The binder reports two 775pro intake motors with 5:1 reduction and four sets of 2-inch compliant wheels per side. The wrist has a separate motor, chain reduction, adjustable tensioner, angle encoder and zeroing switch. The stated roller surface speed is approximately 32 ft/s.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Acquire either the 13-inch or 11-inch cube presentation quickly, center it with little driver precision, clamp securely during wrist motion, and score from either side.

### Engineering interpretation

The pickup combines tolerance at the contact with control of the retained pose. Wheel compliance accommodates the covered crate while the wrist removes a drivebase reversal. A new piece can have a different friction/elasticity regime: 32 ft/s is not a universal optimum. More surface speed can add bounce or surface damage without reducing approach time. Separate capture authority from holding authority and from the wrist trajectory. The retained piece, jaw opening and lift pass-through must clear at the same time.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Compare a swept volume of the largest allowed piece in skewed poses against the uprights and bumper. If contact uncertainty remains, use one adjustable jaw fixture and measure capture, retained pose and release rather than build competing complete robots.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Wristed cube intake](../../images/history_2018-254_p14.jpg)

## Continuous lift rigging and partner-load structure

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [12, 13].

### Published construction or code

Pull-up and pull-down Dyneema cable runs act on both sides of the elevator. Spring tensioning addresses changing fleet angle. The binder specifies a 15-inch separation between pull-up runs for cube passage. The elevator gearbox has four 775pros and two ratios; the low ratio serves climbing and the high ratio serves scoring. Bearings react on different tube faces and edges to support moments.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Allow cube passage, rapid full-height travel, and the torsional loads associated with lifting two robots, while keeping the intake low when stowed.

### Engineering interpretation

Continuous rigging, stage mass and counterforce determine which mass the motor lifts at each segment. The two-sided arrangement can reduce racking only if stiffness, alignment and tension remain adequate. A spring tensioner is not a generic cure for incorrect spool tracking, excessive stretch or sharp cable edges. The published travel and climb timings are design goals/source claims, not measurements reproduced here. For an electric-only adaptation, fixed gearing or electric shifting must still deliver a credible scoring/climbing torque-speed envelope.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Derive lift kinematics and force through every travel segment. Check overlap, tube-face contact stress, shaft moments, cable bending radius and tension access; evaluate score and climb loads separately before selecting gearing.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Pass-through elevator](../../images/history_2018-254_p12.jpg)

![Elevator gearbox](../../images/history_2018-254_p13.jpg)

## Hook, forklift and aligned two-robot lift

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [15, 16].

### Published construction or code

A hook pivots from a retained spring-loaded state to a hard stop. Deployable forks support a partner while the elevator/hanger arrangement raises the pair. The binder discusses keeping the combined CG under the bar and allowing a cube through the fork spacing. Cylinders retain or deploy historical components; they are not permitted actuation for a new 1833 recommendation.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Lift a broad range of partners quickly, preserve ordinary scoring passage, and react partner loads without rotating the pair away from the support.

### Engineering interpretation

The partner interface is a structural mechanism, not just two pieces of carbon tube. The load travels from partner underside/bumpers through forks, their pivots and tensile reactions into the elevator/chassis. Docking clearance and partner drive geometry determine whether the “universal” aspiration holds. A no-air redesign needs a positive retained state during violent driving and a repeatable deployed stop. Merely replacing a cylinder with a motor leaves latch release, power loss, backdrive and accidental triggering unresolved.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Draw the complete force diagram and docked support geometry using a worst-case partner envelope. Separate partner approach reliability from winch capacity and test a proof load only after the structural path and safety factors are justified.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Hanging hook and elevator](../../images/history_2018-254_p15.jpg)

![Partner forklift](../../images/history_2018-254_p16.jpg)

## Coordinated transitions, scale sensing and qualification independence

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [6, 7, 18, 19, 20].

### Published construction or code

The software section describes spline trajectory generation. The binder names pure pursuit, while pinned public code defaults to nonlinear feedback. Event deployment remains unresolved, modeled feedforward and a motion planner for intake/wrist/elevator transitions. Gravity and acceleration terms support superstructure control. A driver-station webcam estimates scale angle from the colored arm. The team’s championship report describes selecting combined switch/scale auto when switch scoring by partners was uncertain.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Score early, reduce collision risk inside the superstructure, and position at the necessary scale height rather than always lifting blindly to a fixed maximum.

### Engineering interpretation

A game-state objective maps into several engineering requirements: reliable capture preserves the next path; scale attitude changes required height; an early autonomous lead changes the opponent’s teleop catch-up burden. The camera location and contemporary rules matter. The transferable principle is state-informed motion, not permission to reuse an old off-board sensing arrangement under a new manual. All three line crossings remain partner-dependent even when the robot owns switch scoring.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Define legal transition states and rejection/recovery behavior before coding auto sequences. Use logged target age and mechanism readiness; validate uncertain transitions rather than assume a perfect path simulation proves acquisition.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Scale attitude detection view](../../images/history_2018-254_p20.jpg)

## Remaining evidence gaps

- Curated historical mechanism cohort, not a top-25 EPA selection; no EPA/rank fabricated.
- Selected primary publications and figures reviewed; no narrated-video review or exact CAD verification is claimed.
- Historical pneumatic/turret hardware is retained as fact but disallowed in new 1833 recommendations. Adaptation requires new interface/load/holding/recovery analysis.
- No exhaustive every-version certification, new PCH performance benchmark or match-by-match Einstein tactical audit.

A spring tensioner is not a generic cure for incorrect spool tracking, excessive stretch or sharp cable edges. The published travel and climb timings are design goals/source claims, not measurements reproduced here. For an electric-only adaptation, fixed gearing or electric shifting must still deliver a credible scoring/climbing torque-speed envelope.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Derive lift kinematics and force through every travel segment. Check overlap, tube-face contact stress, shaft moments, cable bending radius and tension access; evaluate score and climb loads separately before selecting gearing.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Pass-through elevator](../../images/history_2018-254_p12.jpg)

![Elevator gearbox](../../images/history_2018-254_p13.jpg)

## Hook, forklift and aligned two-robot lift

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [15, 16].

### Published construction or code

A hook pivots from a retained spring-loaded state to a hard stop. Deployable forks support a partner while the elevator/hanger arrangement raises the pair. The binder discusses keeping the combined CG under the bar and allowing a cube through the fork spacing. Cylinders retain or deploy historical components; they are not permitted actuation for a new 1833 recommendation.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Lift a broad range of partners quickly, preserve ordinary scoring passage, and react partner loads without rotating the pair away from the support.

### Engineering interpretation

The partner interface is a structural mechanism, not just two pieces of carbon tube. The load travels from partner underside/bumpers through forks, their pivots and tensile reactions into the elevator/chassis. Docking clearance and partner drive geometry determine whether the “universal” aspiration holds. A no-air redesign needs a positive retained state during violent driving and a repeatable deployed stop. Merely replacing a cylinder with a motor leaves latch release, power loss, backdrive and accidental triggering unresolved.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Draw the complete force diagram and docked support geometry using a worst-case partner envelope. Separate partner approach reliability from winch capacity and test a proof load only after the structural path and safety factors are justified.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Hanging hook and elevator](../../images/history_2018-254_p15.jpg)

![Partner forklift](../../images/history_2018-254_p16.jpg)

## Coordinated transitions, scale sensing and qualification independence

Version: LOCKDOWN published 2018 configuration. Source: https://media.team254.com/2018/07/8fda07af-2018-Techbinder.pdf. Physical PDF pages: [6, 7, 18, 19, 20].

### Published construction or code

The software section describes spline trajectory generation. The binder names pure pursuit, while pinned public code defaults to nonlinear feedback. Event deployment remains unresolved, modeled feedforward and a motion planner for intake/wrist/elevator transitions. Gravity and acceleration terms support superstructure control. A driver-station webcam estimates scale angle from the colored arm. The team’s championship report describes selecting combined switch/scale auto when switch scoring by partners was uncertain.

### Team rationale or evidence boundary

Score early, reduce collision risk inside the superstructure, and position at the necessary scale height rather than always lifting blindly to a fixed maximum.

### Engineering interpretation

A game-state objective maps into several engineering requirements: reliable capture preserves the next path; scale attitude changes required height; an early autonomous lead changes the opponent’s teleop catch-up burden. The camera location and contemporary rules matter. The transferable principle is state-informed motion, not permission to reuse an old off-board sensing arrangement under a new manual. All three line crossings remain partner-dependent even when the robot owns switch scoring.

### Proposed validation — not performed

Define legal transition states and rejection/recovery behavior before coding auto sequences. Use logged target age and mechanism readiness; validate uncertain transitions rather than assume a perfect path simulation proves acquisition.

### Limits

Team publication and selected figures, not an independent performance test or exhaustive competition chronology. Source dimensions and reported speeds require validation for a new design.

![Scale attitude detection view](../../images/history_2018-254_p20.jpg)

## Remaining evidence gaps

- Curated historical mechanism cohort, not a top-25 EPA selection; no EPA/rank fabricated.
- Selected primary publications and figures reviewed; no narrated-video review or exact CAD verification is claimed.
- Historical pneumatic/turret hardware is retained as fact but disallowed in new 1833 recommendations. Adaptation requires new interface/load/holding/recovery analysis.
- No exhaustive every-version certification, new PCH performance benchmark or match-by-match Einstein tactical audit.

source_reviews.review_basis: Read results and reconcile the four official event subtotals
source_reviews.facts: 53–0–0 in official play. Arizona North 15–0, Silicon Valley 15–0, Hopper 16–0 and Einstein 7–0. Overall 94–6–0 includes offseason.
source_reviews.limitations: Alliance results do not isolate an individual robot or mechanism.

source_reviews.title: Team 254 season page
source_reviews.facts: The six-wheel drive, pass-through lift, wristed acquisition and partner forks are central to the published design.
source_reviews.limitations: Exact deployment and changes require an event-specific source.

source_reviews.title: Lockdown technical binder
source_reviews.review_basis: Binder construction, controls and existing source figures
source_reviews.facts: Lift, drive, cube tool, hook and partner forks are illustrated separately.
source_reviews.limitations: Page figures do not establish complete CAD, collision envelopes or physical verification.

source_reviews.title: Team 254 championship account
source_reviews.facts: The team describes three-to-four scale-cube autonomous routines and a switch-plus-scale alternative. On Einstein, 254 focused on the scale, 148 on the opposing switch and 2976 on defense around the portals.
source_reviews.limitations: Team narrative describes allocation and reported performance.

source_reviews.title: Pinned public DriveMotionPlanner source
source_reviews.review_basis: Static read of pinned Java source
source_reviews.facts: NONLINEAR_FEEDBACK is initialized by default. PURE_PURSUIT is also implemented as a selectable follower.
source_reviews.limitations: The public release is distinct from a verified Houston deployment.

source_reviews.title: Team 254 code release discussion
source_reviews.locator: Announcement and team reply on cube release
source_reviews.facts: The release describes nonlinear following and spline trajectories. The team describes a low-power withdrawal option for crowded cube placement.
source_reviews.limitations: The published explanation does not provide a measured placement-rate comparison.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Lockdown went 53–0–0 across official 2018 competition. The machine made a large part of POWER UP a repeatable cube cycle: acquire directly into a wristed intake, retain the cube while raising it, then place it on either side of the lift. A two-speed six-wheel chassis gave the driver a separate tool for short approaches and longer traversals. A partner lift shared the vertical structure but created a different load case from ordinary scoring. At Houston the team varied autonomous tasks with alliance capability and used coordinated scale, switch and defensive roles. That combination of packaging, controls and alliance execution is essential to understanding the record.
piece_flow: The opposed rollers take possession directly at the front. The jaws constrain the cube as it is lifted, so the robot does not release it into an intermediate conveyor.

The carriage and wrist move to a feasible scoring pose. Clear space in the elevator lets the retained cube pass through and exit toward the rear when that route saves a chassis turn. The controls coordinate those motions to protect the cube and structure.
Near a crowded stack, the robot can release more gently and withdraw rather than opening the jaws wide into adjacent pieces. Then the wrist and lift return to a low acquisition pose.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The six-wheel base packages drive gearboxes and electrical hardware low. Two open lift uprights guide the carriage without filling the central passage used by the cube. At layout scale, that passage must fit the cube’s diagonal, tool contacts, wrist sweep and deflected cable runs together. Carrying the cube high changes wheel loading and makes abrupt lateral corrections more consequential. The late-match hook and partner forks route forces back into the lift and chassis, so their supporting structure and stow envelope are part of the original concept.

subsystems.name: Two-speed drivetrain
subsystems.construction: Six-wheel differential chassis with compact gearboxes and low-mounted hardware.
subsystems.operation: Select the useful ratio for the route and preserve a predictable approach while the elevator moves.
subsystems.team_rationale: Short-cycle acceleration and driving across the field impose different demands.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A repeatable stopping pose makes the wrist and lift more useful. A faster top speed matters only where the route gives room to accelerate and decelerate.
subsystems.interfaces: Lift reactions and partner loads pass through the chassis. Driver approach heading interacts with the choice of front or rear release.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: A frame hit can change approach accuracy without obvious failure in the scoring hardware. Inspect gearbox and wheel retention after contact.
subsystems.unknowns: Source-reported speed is not loaded measured cycle performance.

subsystems.name: Roller intake and wrist
subsystems.construction: Opposed powered roller groups on a wristed cube manipulator with movable jaws.
subsystems.operation: Acquire from the floor, retain the cube while the wrist rotates, then drop or eject at the target.
subsystems.team_rationale: Front and rear releases widen the useful scoring poses.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Maintaining possession across transit removes a transfer boundary. The mouth still needs to tolerate off-center cubes and the hold geometry must survive reversal and acceleration.
subsystems.interfaces: The cube envelope, wrist linkage and jaw opening compete for the same pass-through opening.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: A loaded cube can move under reversal or crowding. Gentle release is a separate operating condition from maximum ejection.
subsystems.unknowns: No complete tested capture envelope or independently measured hold reliability is available.

subsystems.name: Pass-through elevator
subsystems.construction: Two-stage lift with rigging and a clear center between the lift rails.
subsystems.operation: Raise the same cube tool to the target, then lower it and restore the floor pickup pose.
subsystems.team_rationale: One structure serves multiple scoring heights and works with the reversible tool.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A short mechanical path still requires careful motion planning. Rail spacing, cable pretension and torsion become more important if the tool is extended and the piece sits off center.
subsystems.interfaces: The clear passage also needs room for cable motion and harness bend radius, while the elevator is the structural support for endgame loads.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check carriage binding, rigging wear and access to replace a cable without stripping unrelated mechanisms.
subsystems.unknowns: Source figures establish arrangement and selected dimensions, with dynamic deflection and friction unresolved.

subsystems.name: Hook and partner forks
subsystems.construction: Upper hook and deployable fork assembly integrated with the scoring lift.
subsystems.operation: Enter the climbing configuration, engage the bar and support an alliance partner when the setup allows.
subsystems.team_rationale: The endgame function made use of the same major lifting structure.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Shared hardware saves a separate lift volume, but it raises design loads and demands a distinct mode. Partner geometry and alignment can dominate endgame reliability.
subsystems.interfaces: Bar, hook, carriage, forks and frame make one coupled load path. Folded hardware cannot obstruct normal cube cycles.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check fork alignment, unequal partner loading and whether the driver can abandon a slow setup.
subsystems.unknowns: No universal partner fit or verified safety factor follows from published renderings.

subsystems.name: Controls and autonomous
subsystems.construction: Spline trajectory following, coordinated lift and wrist commands, and a scale-attitude sensing account.
subsystems.operation: Schedule acquisition and lift states around the route, then release once possession and pose allow. Choose autonomous tasks with partner capability in mind.
subsystems.team_rationale: A useful start required early cube scoring and enough flexibility to cover uncertain switch capability.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The closest transfer is making possession, target pose and return path explicit. Copying a controller does little if the robot cannot repeat the physical transition it is commanding.
subsystems.interfaces: A path can pass only if the tool and cube clear the route at the actual lift and wrist states.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: A missed acquisition or stale target estimate needs an explicit fallback. End-stop and transition checks need validation with the actual mechanism.
subsystems.unknowns: The binder names pure pursuit. The pinned release defaults to nonlinear feedback. The Houston binary remains unauthenticated.

revisions: Official competition and offseason records are separate.
Binder and public code preserve different software evidence. Avoid assigning the public release default to every event.
transferable_principles: Keep the cube in one tool when that tool can reach pickup and scoring poses with acceptable approach tolerance.
Trade robot yaw against tool motion using measured complete cycles, including recovery from poor pickups and crowded targets.
Give qualification autonomous routines enough independent scoring capability to remain useful with unfamiliar partners.
disconfirming_conditions: A dedicated wide collector may win if approach error dominates cycle time and a reliable transfer is available.
Front and rear release lose value when routes or field access force a consistent chassis heading.
A shared endgame lift loses value if its structural and access costs reduce the primary scoring rate.
remaining_gaps: Exact event-by-event hardware and code configurations, measured cycle-time distribution, loaded deflection, partner compatibility and field-aligned failure rates.
